scene.headline: Adobe ends Creative Suite, goes subscription-only

lines.text: Top bundle, CS6 Master Collection: $2,599 once, vs. $49.99 a month.
lines.say: The top bundle, Creative Suite six Master Collection, was two thousand five hundred ninety-nine dollars once, versus about fifty dollars a month.
At those prices, renting passes the purchase price in about fifty-two months.
From fiscal twenty twenty to twenty twenty-five, subscription revenue roughly doubled to about twenty-two point nine billion dollars.

lines.text: Signed but not yet counted: $22.52B at the end of fiscal 2025.
lines.say: By the end of fiscal twenty twenty-five, another twenty-two and a half billion was already signed but not yet counted.
One more copy costs almost nothing, so gross margin was about eighty-nine percent.

lines.text: At the 2013 price, $49.99 a month = about $600 a year.

post.title: 96% of Adobe's Revenue Is Subscriptions. Here's Why
post.ig:
You can't buy Photoshop anymore. You rent it.
96% of Adobe's fiscal 2025 revenue came from subscriptions.
In 2013, Adobe swapped its top $2,599 Creative Suite bundle for Creative Cloud at $49.99 a month.
Subscription revenue grew from $11.6B in fiscal 2020 to $22.9B in fiscal 2025.
It also had $22.52B in signed contracts not yet counted as revenue (as of Nov. 28, 2025), and an 89% gross margin in fiscal 2025.
Sources: Adobe 10-K filings FY2020-FY2025, TechCrunch (May 2013).
